'''William Bradshaw Amos''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 1945)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Amos, William Bradshaw (Brad) | id = U245920 | year = 2017 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U245920 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref><ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/william-amos-10988|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117110025/https://royalsociety.org/people/william-amos-10988|archive-date=2015-11-17|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=Royal Society|location=London|author=Anon|year=2007|title=Dr William Amos FRS}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref> is a British [[biologist]], Emeritus Scientist at the [[Medical Research Council (UK)|Medical Research Council]] (MRC) [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] (LMB).<ref>{{cite web|author=UK |url=http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/group-leaders/emeritus-scientists |title=Emeritus - MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology |website=Mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk |date=2014-06-20 |access-date=2016-12-29}}</ref> He led a team that developed the mesolens, a [[microscope]] with a giant lens.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/group-leaders/emeritus-scientists/b-amos |title=Brad Amos |website=www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110923103029/http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/group-leaders/emeritus-scientists/b-amos |archive-date=2011-09-23}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mrc.ac.uk/Newspublications/News/MRC006930 |title=Medical Research Council - News - MRC scientists develop new giant lens |website=www.mrc.ac.uk |access-date=12 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120418193129/http://www.mrc.ac.uk/Newspublications/News/MRC006930 |archive-date=18 April 2012 }}</ref><ref name=elife>{{Cite journal|last1=McConnell|first1=Gail|author-link1=Gail McConnell|last2=Trägårdh|first2=Johanna|last3=Amor|first3=Rumelo|last4=Dempster|first4=John|last5=Reid|first5=Es|last6=Amos|first6=William Bradshaw|date=2016|title=A novel optical microscope for imaging large embryos and tissue volumes with sub-cellular resolution throughout|journal=eLife|volume=5|article-number=e18659|doi=10.7554/eLife.18659|issn=2050-084X|pmid=27661778 |pmc=5035146 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Education==
Amos was educated at [[King Edward VII School, Sheffield]]<ref name=whoswho/> and graduated from [[University of Oxford]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in 1966, and from [[University of Cambridge]] with a [[PhD]] in 1970.<ref name=wphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|first=William Bradshaw|last=Amos|publisher=University of Cambridge|title= Aspects of contraction in the Peritrich stalk|year=1975|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.447807}}|oclc=1064544089|url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/23482317?style=html|website=jisc.ac.uk}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Amos was research assistant from 1966 to 1967, research student from 1967 to 1970, and [[research fellow]] from 1970 to 1974 at [[King's College, Cambridge]]. He taught at the department of zoology, Cambridge, from 1973 to 1978.<ref name=whoswho/>

===Awards and honours===
His awards and honours include:

*1994 [[Mullard Award]] of the [[Royal Society]]{{citation needed|date=March 2019}}
*1995 [[Rank Prize for Optoelectronics]]<ref name=optfund>{{cite web  | title=Past Prizes in Optoelectronics | website=The Rank Prize Funds | url=http://www.rankprize.org/index.php/prizes/optoelectronics | access-date=11 July 2020}}</ref> 
*2002 Progress Medal of the [[Royal Photographic Society]]{{citation needed|date=March 2019}}
*2002 Ernst Abbe Award for Lifetime Achievement of the New York Microscopical Society{{citation needed|date=March 2019}}
